In that load's callback filterKey.current is undefined, so setFilters(readReviewFilters(key)) runs (:233-236) in the same async callback as setRead({ scope: 'open/', snapshot }) (:241); React 18 batches both, so the next render already has the saved scope (e.g. 'merged/' or 'open/7'), snapshot is null because read.scope !== scope (:276), the attentionPrs memo returns carriedAttention unchanged (:339-348) and the write-back effect does nothing (:351). The open snapshot is never shown and nothing is written back, while the callback's only write to the carried set is the reset (:231). The next load for the saved scope has replaceAttention false (same identity; merged/closed or a period, :230), so the carried set stays empty unless the shown snapshot itself holds the card; a merged or closed load never holds an open pull request, and a period load holds it only when it was updated within the period. At 33fd9647a the callback judged the loaded cards into the carried set (:231-238 there), so this is a behaviour change introduced by the F-015 fix in this branch (cc42698a3), whose commit message says only that 'the load only decides whether to reset the carried set' and records no decision about hidden first loads; the base comment at :229 ('cannot replace the open snapshot') argues for keeping the open requests, not for dropping them. No intent signal or practice source stands against the finding, and the suggested fix (seed on a replacing load, keep the memo and the write-back) restores the earlier behaviour without undoing F-015's removal persistence. Noted, not a premise change: for a saved period on the open state the miss is narrower (only open pull requests not updated within the period).
